code: set.seed(1)  # Two tests, verification depending only on the results (MAR): subjects # negative to both tests are verified with probability 0.1, the others with # probability 0.9 or 1. The profiles are in the order (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1). d <- simulate_study(n = 500, prevalence = 0.2,                     sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.7),                     specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),                     verification_prob = c(0.1, 0.9, 0.9, 1)) head(d) #>   A B verified disease #> 1 0 0        0      NA #> 2 0 0        0      NA #> 3 0 0        0      NA #> 4 1 0        1       1 #> 5 0 0        0      NA #> 6 0 1        1       1 # proportion of verified subjects by profile tapply(d$verified, paste(d$A, d$B), mean) #>       0 0       0 1       1 0       1 1  #> 0.1057402 0.8333333 0.9078947 1.0000000   # Everyone verified: a single verification probability equal to 1 d_full <- simulate_study(n = 500, prevalence = 0.2,                          sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.7),                          specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),                          verification_prob = 1) mean(d_full$verified) #> [1] 1  # A never-verified profile: only subjects positive to at least one test are # verified, so the disease status is missing for every (0,0) subject d_screen <- simulate_study(n = 500, prevalence = 0.2,                            sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.7),                            specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),                            verification_prob = c(0, 1, 1, 1)) table(paste(d_screen$A, d_screen$B), d_screen$verified) #>       #>         0   1 #>   0 0 305   0 #>   0 1   0  23 #>   1 0   0  99 #>   1 1   0  73  # Verification that depends on the disease (MNAR): with odds_ratio = 3 the # odds of verification are three times higher for the diseased, so among # the verified the diseased are over-represented d_mnar <- simulate_study(n = 5000, prevalence = 0.2,                          sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.7),                          specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),                          verification_prob = 0.3, odds_ratio = 3) mean(d_mnar$disease, na.rm = TRUE)   # well above the prevalence 0.2 #> [1] 0.3348066  # Three tests without names: the columns are called T1, T2, T3, and there # are 2^3 = 8 profiles, so verification_prob has 8 values d3 <- simulate_study(n = 500, prevalence = 0.1,                      sensitivity = c(0.9, 0.8, 0.7),                      specificity = c(0.9, 0.9, 0.95),                      verification_prob = c(0.05, rep(0.8, 6), 1)) names(d3) #> [1] "T1"       "T2"       "T3"       "verified" "disease"   # Three tests dependent given the disease: among the diseased tests A and B # share a latent severity, C much less; among the healthy only A and B # are (weakly) dependent d_dep <- simulate_study(n = 5000, prevalence = 0.2,                         sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8, C = 0.7),                         specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.9, C = 0.95),                         verification_prob = c(0.05, rep(0.8, 6), 1),                         dependence = latent_dependence(                           diseased_loadings = c(1, 1, 0.3),                           healthy_loadings = c(0.5, 0.5, 0))) sick <- which(d_dep$disease == 1) cor(d_dep[sick, c("A", "B", "C")]) #>            A          B          C #> A 1.00000000 0.10113242 0.02708195 #> B 0.10113242 1.00000000 0.07264363 #> C 0.02708195 0.07264363 1.00000000  # Correlation 0.4 between every pair of tests among the diseased and -0.2 # among the healthy d_probit <- simulate_study(n = 5000, prevalence = 0.2,                            sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8, C = 0.7),                            specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.9, C = 0.95),                            verification_prob = 1,                            dependence = probit_dependence(                              diseased_correlation = 0.4,                              healthy_correlation = -0.2))
